Why quotes vary

  
    
    
  • Window count and panes — pricing is per window ($8–$16 inside + out), and multi-pane French windows carry more panes per unit.
    • 
    
  • Stories and access — second- and third-story glass needs ladders, poles, or lifts, and takes longer per window.
    • 
    
  • Inside + out vs. exterior only — exterior-only roughly halves the per-window rate ($4–$8) and the median job ($180 vs. $228).
    • 
    
  • Condition — hard-water stains, paint overspray, and years of buildup are restoration work, not a standard clean.
    • 
    
  • Add-ons — screens, tracks, sills, and skylights are extra panes of work; expect them itemized on a proper quote.
    • 
    
  • Frequency — most homes book 2–4 visits a year; a standing schedule keeps each visit at the standard clean rate instead of a first-time deep clean.
    • 
  






  
Window cleaning services & what each one costs

  
The main jobs homeowners search for, priced from the same 2026 figures above. Find your job, note its fair band, then run it through the estimator.


  

    

      
Residential whole-house window cleaning

      
The full visit: every window in the home, inside + out. For the average ~22-window home this is the $221 average / $150–$303 typical job (Angi). Housecall Pro's whole-property inside + out median is $228.

      
Best for: annual or twice-yearly full cleans, move-ins, and pre-sale prep.

    

    

      
Exterior-only window cleaning

      
Outside glass only, usually with water-fed poles from the ground. At $4–$8 per window and a $180 median whole-property job, it is the budget-friendly maintenance clean between full visits.

      
Best for: upkeep between deep cleans; homes where interior glass stays clean.

    

    

      
Interior + exterior window cleaning

      
Both faces of the glass, plus interior detailing. At $8–$16 per window it costs roughly double exterior-only — and it is the only way to remove interior film, cooking grease haze, and pet nose-prints.

      
Best for: spring cleaning, allergies, selling a home, holiday hosting.

    

    

      
Screens, tracks & sills

      
The detail work a glass-only clean skips: screens removed and washed, tracks vacuumed and wiped, sills cleaned. On this page's estimator these are priced at the published $4–$8 per-pane rate — ask for them as separate line items on any quote.

      
Best for: windows that get opened often; pollen and dust-prone regions.

    

    

      
Hard-water stain removal

      
Sprinkler overspray and mineral-heavy water etch white deposits into glass that a standard clean cannot shift. Stain treatment is restoration work priced per affected pane — get it quoted separately, in writing, before work starts.

      
Best for: homes with lawn sprinklers hitting glass; well-water areas.

    

    

      
Skylight cleaning

      
Skylights collect roof grit and pollen and are easy to forget — until the drip stains show. Pros price them as extra high-access panes; include your skylight count in the estimator so quotes cover them from the start.

      
Best for: vaulted living rooms, loft conversions, sunrooms.

    

    

      
High windows & second-story glass

      
Two- and three-story glass is where DIY gets dangerous and pros earn their rate: ladders, water-fed poles, and safety gear. Expect quotes toward the top of the per-window range — the Housecall Pro inside + out range runs to $395 for larger, taller properties.

      
Best for: 2–3 story homes, foyer and stairwell glass, clerestory windows.

    

    

      
Storefront & commercial glass

      
Shops, cafés, and offices usually buy recurring storefront cleaning on a route schedule rather than a per-visit residential rate. Use the quote pack format to describe pane count and frequency, and ask for a per-visit and per-month price in writing.

      
Best for: retail fronts, restaurants, showrooms, low-rise offices.

    

    

      
Gutter-adjacent exterior cleaning

      
Window visits often pair with the exterior jobs around them — clearing the glass after gutter overflow, washing soffits and frames streaked by dirty runoff. Describe it in the pack notes so one visit can cover glass and the staining above it.

      
Best for: post-storm cleanups; homes with overflowing gutters streaking the glass.

    

    

      
Recurring seasonal cleaning

      
Most homes book 2–4 visits per year. A spring + fall schedule keeps each visit a standard clean at standard rates — leave it for years and the first visit back is priced like the restoration job it has become.

      
Best for: tree-heavy lots, dusty or coastal areas, rental properties between tenants.

    

  


  





  
Choosing a window cleaner you can trust

  

    

      
Window cleaning is unlicensed in most states, so your questions are the quality filter. Ask every firm these before you book:

      
    
        
  • "Are you insured?" — liability cover is the baseline for anyone working on ladders around your home.
    • 
        
  • "What's included in the per-window price?" — glass only, or frames, screens, tracks, and sills too? Compare the answer with the bands on this page.
    • 
        
  • "Is the quote per window, per pane, or flat?" — any structure is fine if it is written and itemized before work starts.
    • 
        
  • "How do you reach second-story glass?" — ladders, water-fed poles, or lifts — and is that priced in?
    • 
        
  • "What if you find hard-water damage or a broken seal?" — you want photos and a separate written price, not surprise add-ons mid-job.
    • 
      

      
Red flags: a quote far above $303 for an average home with no explanation, cash-only with no invoice, or a "free clean" that turns into a hard sell. There is no dominant dedicated window-cleaning quote brand in the US — Angi, HomeAdvisor, and Thumbtack are general marketplaces — so a clear written quote from a local firm, checked against the table above, is your best protection.

    

    
  






  
Storefront & commercial window cleaning

  

    
    

      
Commercial glass is quoted differently from homes: by pane count, frontage, access, and visit frequency on a route. The residential per-window bands on this page do not transfer directly — but the quote pack does. Use the estimator form to describe your property, set frequency to the schedule you want, and note the storefront details (pane count, frontage, opening hours) in the notes field.

      
    
        
  • Ask for per-visit and per-month pricing — route discounts only show up when both are written down.
    • 
        
  • Specify inside, outside, or both — display glass usually needs both faces.
    • 
        
  • Confirm early-morning slots — most storefront work happens before opening.
    •

Frequently asked questions

  
How much does window cleaning cost in the USA in 2026?
The national average is $221 per visit, with a typical range of $150–$303 per visit (Angi, based on 25,969 verified projects, updated October 8, 2026). Per window, expect $8–$16 for inside + out cleaning and $4–$8 for exterior only.

  
How much does it cost per window?
Inside + out runs $8–$16 per window; exterior only runs $4–$8 per window; per pane is $4–$8 (Housecall Pro October 2026 guide, citing Angi/HomeAdvisor). Housecall Pro's price-book median for a whole property is $228 inside + out and $180 exterior only.

  
How many windows does an average home have?
About 22 windows (EPA, June 2026). At $8–$16 per window inside + out, a typical 22-window home lands near the $221 national average per visit.

  
How often should windows be professionally cleaned?
Most homes book 2–4 times per year. Twice a year (spring and fall) is the common baseline; homes under heavy tree cover, near construction, or in dusty or coastal areas often book quarterly.

  
Is exterior-only window cleaning worth it?
Yes for many homes: exterior-only costs $4–$8 per window versus $8–$16 inside + out, and Housecall Pro's median exterior-only job is $180 versus $228 inside + out. Choose inside + out when interior glass, tracks, and sills are visibly dirty or before selling a home.

  
Does this page send my details to window cleaners?
No. This page sends nothing to any cleaner. The estimator and quote request pack run entirely in your browser; you download, copy, or email the pack yourself to any local firm you choose. Firm matching is a future launch model only and is not active on this page.

  
What is the minimum charge for window cleaning?
Most pros set a minimum charge of $75–$250 per visit, and hourly rates run $45–$75 per cleaner. Small jobs are usually billed at the minimum rather than the per-window rate.
